variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A real-time analytics system continuously turns events into recent metrics, features, predictions, or actions within a declared freshness deadline. Unlike a batch job, it must reason about event time, late and duplicate data, state recovery, backpressure, and how partial failure changes the result.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Event time
pairs.detail: Use source timestamps for windows when network or processing delay would otherwise assign an event to the wrong period.
pairs.explanation: Use source timestamps for windows when network or processing delay would otherwise assign an event to the wrong period.

pairs.label: Watermark
pairs.detail: Estimate how complete event-time progress is.
pairs.explanation: Estimate how complete event-time progress is. The allowed-lateness policy trades lower delay for fewer corrections.

pairs.label: State and checkpoint
pairs.detail: Window aggregates, joins, and model features need durable snapshots tied to input positions so a restart can reproduce results.
pairs.explanation: Window aggregates, joins, and model features need durable snapshots tied to input positions so a restart can reproduce results.

pairs.label: Idempotent effect
pairs.detail: Use stable event and result keys so retries or replay do not double-charge, double-alert, or corrupt an aggregate.
pairs.explanation: Use stable event and result keys so retries or replay do not double-charge, double-alert, or corrupt an aggregate.

variants.hint:
Event time: Use source timestamps for windows when network or processing delay would otherwise assign an event to the wrong period.

Watermark: Estimate how complete event-time progress is.

State and checkpoint: Window aggregates, joins, and model features need durable snapshots tied to input positions so a restart can reproduce results.

Idempotent effect: Use stable event and result keys so retries or replay do not double-charge, double-alert, or corrupt an aggregate.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.
